verdicts.quote: Promotion is automatic, in first-come order**, with no claim window or hold timer.

first-come-first-served by the server's recorded join order … two joins that arrive "simultaneously" are totally ordered by the server's single recorded sequence … Out of scope for this R: waitlist cap (G-3), guests/group joins, paid or priority waitlists.
promotion applies the same booking rules a direct booking would (G-1 lists them: e.g. account in good standing, credits/payment, time conflicts).
verdicts.missing: After confirming one class, should the system immediately remove the member from the overlapping waitlist or check the conflict only when the second seat opens?

verdicts.quote: how credits, payment, cancellation penalties apply to a promoted booking. Assumed: same rules as a direct booking at promotion time.
verdicts.missing: Automatic promotion has no offer to decline. The spec leaves unstated whether missing the promoted class counts as a no-show, including when the member misses the notice.

verdicts.quote: when a confirmed booking on a full class ends (member cancels, staff cancels it) … the code path that cancels a booking (or raises capacity) calls one shared promote-next routine inside the same transaction

the app's existing booking-confirmation channel plus in-app status … "You're in: Spin 18:00" … notification provider rejects the send → `cy` is still *Confirmed*; a retry later delivers exactly one notice.
two freed seats promote two, in order … confirmed ≤ capacity … each freed seat promotes at most one member exactly once even if the cancel event is retried.
Direct bookers cannot take that seat ahead of the waitlist. … each member has at most one entry or booking per class … a losing concurrent request gets the normal rejection (full / already booked)

same rules as a direct booking at promotion time … A head-of-list member who fails them is removed from the waitlist with a reason, notified (R-6), and the next member is tried. … a skipped member is not charged

verdicts.missing: The default allows unlimited joins. If the open cap decision yields a limit, its value and the message a member sees when it is reached remain unspecified.

verdicts.quote: no promotion occurs, once the class can no longer be booked: at the same cutoff that applies to direct bookings, or at the class start time if there is none
capacity raised 2→4 while waitlist is `[cy, dee, eli]` and 2 confirmed → `cy` and `dee` promoted (in that order), `eli` remains position 1, count 4/4.
verdicts.missing: If staff lower capacity below the confirmed count, the builder must decide whether to reject the change or adjust bookings and what happens to queue order if members are displaced.

verdicts.quote: If a class is cancelled or removed, all its waitlist entries end and members are notified.

Waitlist entry data = member id, class id, join sequence, created-at. … Kept: until the entry ends (promoted → becomes a booking; left/removed/expired → deleted). … Positions are 1-based and contiguous.
entries are never silently left dangling past the class's end. … Kept: until the entry ends (promoted → becomes a booking; left/removed/expired → deleted). No separate history is retained
a member sees only their own position, never other members' identities
staff views of waitlists are not requested and out of scope (G-7). … No waitlist history is kept
verdicts.missing: Staff visibility and history are explicitly excluded. The spec provides no staff workflow for choosing a member to promote or remove, or for looking up who was promoted when.

verdicts.quote: the earliest eligible waitlisted member is given a confirmed booking for the freed seat, in the same atomic step as the seat being freed.

everything the app does today for non-full classes, cancellations, rosters, attendance, capacity counts, billing/credits and reports is unchanged. A waitlist entry occupies no seat … a non-full class: book, cancel, rebook flows behave as before this change.
